quote:
The auto etl run pipeline has three data-source phases — sessions, git,
and github. The git and github phases currently discover which repositories
to index by reading the remotes cache (~/.auto/etl/settings.json), a map of
workspace paths to remote URLs that is built organically each time the sessions
phase runs.
Because the sessions phase scans every directory under ~/.claude/projects/, the
remotes cache accumulates every repo Claude has ever opened — including random
GitHub projects pulled in briefly to research a problem. The git phase then
indexes every commit in all those repos, and the github phase tries to sync PRs
from all of them, polluting the parquet output with large volumes of unrelated
project data.
The registry needed to fix this already exists: ~/.auto/projects.json
(ProjectsConfig in auto-shared/config/projects.go) is the canonical host-level
project registry, already used by auto-watch, auto-skill, and auto-cli init --project.
The ETL pipeline simply does not use it yet.

quote:
When the project registry is empty and `--repo-path` is not provided, should the
`git` and `github` phases:
(a) warn on stderr and skip gracefully (non-fatal, matching current github behaviour), or
(b) return a hard error (exit non-zero)?

The recommended answer is (a) warn-and-skip when running all sources by default,
but return a hard error when `--only git` or `--only github` is passed explicitly
(matching the existing `explicitOnly` pattern already in `runGitHubSync`).

quote:
Table.insert(..., pk='id', ignore=True) raises an IndexError when the SQLite
connection has previously written rows to a different table. After an INSERT OR IGNORE
that skips a duplicate row, result.lastrowid is non-zero (it reflects the last successful
insert across the entire connection), so the guard if self.last_rowid is truthy. The code
then queries rowid = result.lastrowid against the target table — which never had a row
with that rowid — and [0] on an empty list raises IndexError.
Affected code: sqlite_utils/db.py line 4390–4392.
